name: S01 push: the first newline of the chunk, not the last
why: the lines after the first newline of a chunk wait in the tail until a later push; a marker line that is the second line of its chunk answers one push late; killed by the named case 'a first Browse at that fails the pattern, then a real one, in one chunk' and by every enumeration

name: S02 push: the end of the completed text is one place too far
why: a chunk with no newline has `end` 1 and is cut, and the first character after a newline is tested with the lines and lost from the tail; killed by the named cases that cut a marker, a URL or an escape

name: S03 push: no +1, so a newline at index 0 reads as no newline
why: a chunk with no newline gets `end` -1 (not 0), a chunk that is only a newline gets 0 and is kept as a tail; killed by the named case 'a URL line whose newline has not arrived, then the newline' and by every enumeration

name: S04 push: the no-newline test is `end <= 0`
why: EQUIVALENT: `end` is `lastIndexOf(...) + 1`, and `lastIndexOf` returns -1 or more, so `end` is 0 or more and `end <= 0` and `end === 0` are the same test

name: S05 push: a chunk that STARTS with a newline counts as having none
why: a chunk that is only a newline (end 1) is kept as a tail and answers null, so a URL line completed by a lone newline answers one push late; killed by 'a URL line whose newline has not arrived, then the newline', the CRLF case cut between CR and LF and every enumeration

name: S06 push: the no-newline branch is taken for `end === 1`
why: a chunk with no newline goes through the completion path, which REPLACES the kept tail by the chunk, and a chunk that is only a newline is kept; killed by the named cut-marker and cut-URL cases

name: S07 push: a chunk with no newline REPLACES the kept tail
why: the pieces received so far are dropped, so a line that arrives in three or more chunks is read from its last piece only; killed by the live capture one character at a time and in pieces of seven

name: S08 push: a chunk with no newline is put BEFORE the kept pieces
why: the pieces of a line are joined in reverse order; killed by the live capture one character at a time and in pieces of seven (three or more pieces), and by every enumeration with a cut in the middle

name: S09 push: a chunk with no newline is parsed with all the pieces joined (the answer is the same, the cost is not)
why: the answer is the same (the joined tail has no newline, and a match needs one, so it is always null) but every push re-joins and re-reads the whole incomplete line: ONE line of 16 MiB in 4,096-character chunks and 256 KiB in one-byte chunks are quadratic again; killed by the clock rows alone

name: S10 push: the kept text goes AFTER the new lines
why: the kept tail is appended to the completed lines instead of starting them; killed by the cut-marker, cut-URL and cut-escape cases

name: S11 push: the pieces are joined with a blank
why: a blank appears at every cut of the incomplete line, so a URL or an escape cut across two chunks is torn; killed by the cut-URL and cut-escape cases

name: S12 push: the whole chunk is tested, not only up to its last newline
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer: the part of the chunk after its last newline has no newline, and a match ends on a newline, so it cannot start, end or extend a match; it is tested a second time later, when its own newline arrives, with the same result; the cost is at most one more read of each byte of a tail

name: S13 push: the last character of the completed text (the newline) is cut
why: the newline that ends every match is cut off, so nothing ever matches; killed by every case that expects a URL

name: S14 push: the first character of the new lines is cut
why: the first character of every chunk with a newline is lost; killed by the cut-marker case (the chunk 'se at ...' loses its s) and by the enumerations

name: S15 push: the incomplete tail of a chunk is dropped
why: the text after the last newline of a chunk is lost, so a marker line that starts in one chunk and ends in the next is never seen; killed by 'noise, then a marker line cut in the middle' and by the enumerations

name: S16 push: the tail is kept also when it is empty
why: EQUIVALENT: for `end === chunk.length` the kept piece is the empty string, and an empty piece joins to nothing

name: S17 push: a tail of one character is dropped
why: a chunk that ends one character after its last newline loses that character; killed by the enumerations (a chunk cut one character after a newline) and by 'the pieces of seven'

name: S18 push: the kept tail starts one character late
why: the first character after the last newline is lost; killed by 'noise, then a marker line cut in the middle' and by the enumerations

name: S19 push: the kept tail starts one character early, with the newline
why: EQUIVALENT: the kept text then starts with the newline that ended the last line, so the next completed text starts with one more EMPTY line; a match cannot start or end on an empty line, and a pattern with no anchor finds the same match, at the same place shifted by one

name: S20 push: a chunk that ends on a newline keeps the old tail
why: the pieces that were just tested stay and are joined in front of the next lines: the cost grows with the stream, and a 'Browse at ' that ended a line is glued to the start of the next one (a false URL); killed by the enumerations, the seeded row and the clock rows

name: S21 push: the tail starts with one empty piece
why: EQUIVALENT: an empty piece joins to nothing

name: S22 push: only the chunk is parsed
why: the kept tail is ignored, so a marker cut across two chunks is never seen; killed by the cut-marker, cut-URL and CRLF-cut cases

name: S23 push: only the new tail is parsed
why: the completed lines are not read at all; killed by every case that expects a URL

name: S24 push: a chunk with no newline is concatenated to the kept text at once
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer and in the cost: the concatenation of strings is a rope in V8 and `join` of one element returns it unflattened, so no push reads the line; the single flatten is at the newline, as before
